profile.entities: Magadh Sugar & Energy Limited; K.K. Birla Group

bull_bear.body: Diversified revenue streams contribute to resilience
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- A dividend of 125%, i.e. Rs. 12.5 per equity share of Rs. 10 each, for 2025-26 was paid on 1 August 2026 - recommended by the Board and approved by shareholders at the AGM.
- Total debt stood at Rs. 482 Cr as at Jun-26 (Term Loan Rs. 248 Cr, Cash Credit/WCDL Rs. 234 Cr) versus Rs. 511 Cr at Jun-25 (216 / 295) and Rs. 691 Cr at Mar-26 (271 / 420).
- Stock position as on 30 June 2026 was Rs. 379 Cr (sugar stock Rs. 293 Cr, molasses / ethanol / other stocks Rs. 86 Cr) versus Rs. 456 Crores as on 30 June 2025.
- Shareholding as on 30 June 2026: promoters 61%, individual/HUF 30%, others including NRIs 9%; free float 39%, market cap Rs. 647 Cr, free-float market cap Rs. 252 Cr on 1.41 Cr shares outstanding.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Sugar and energy segments contribute to revenue
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Incorporated in 1932, with the group in the sugar business for over nine decades; the present company was formed in 2015 pursuant to a scheme of merger and demerger, manufacturing sugar, ethanol and power.
- Deck claims integrated operations across Sugar, Distillery and Co-Gen, patronage of the K.K. Birla Group (established in 1932 by Late Dr. Krishna Kumar Birla), excellent corporate governance, highly experienced management, healthy financials and sustainable EBITDA.
- Long-term credit rating upgraded to A+ by India Ratings and Research Pvt Ltd on 08 May 2026.
- Entirely Bihar-based footprint across Paschim Champaran, Gopalganj and Samastipur; the deck notes Bihar's sugar industry is shifting from simply operating existing mills towards revival, modernisation and integrated sugar-ethanol-power projects.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [FRP] The Government raised the Sugarcane FRP for SS 2026-27 by 2.81% to Rs. 365/qtl, up from Rs. 355/qtl.
- [Bihar policy] Bihar approved the Sugarcane Industry Investment Promotion Policy 2026 to attract fresh investment and modernise sugar mills, ethanol/distilleries and co-generation/power projects; revival of closed sugar mills remains a government priority. Bihar's SS 2025-26 sugar output is reported at around 5.8 LMT versus approximately 6.1 LMT the previous season.
- [Ethanol policy] Ethanol blending reached 20% as on 30 June 2026 (ESY 21-22: 10.02%, 22-23: 12.00%, 23-24: 14.60%, 24-25: 19.17%); NITI Aayog, with an inter-ministerial group, is working on a roadmap for blending targets beyond E20.
- [Industry balance - company estimates] SS 2025-26 estimated: opening stock 47 LMT, production 278 LMT, total availability 325 LMT, domestic consumption 270 LMT, exports 8 LMT, closing stock 47 LMT (about two months of domestic consumption); the Government has indicated any SS 2026-27 export decision will depend on production estimates after the monsoon assessment, likely around September 2026.
- [Key risks] Monsoon variability and possible El Nino impact, delay in export permissions, regulatory intervention if sugar prices rise sharply, revision in ethanol pricing, and increases in FRP or SAP without corresponding sugar price increases.
- [Transformative agenda] Five pillars - Digitalisation of Operations, Rising Capital Expenditure, Governance, Systems-oriented ('Magadh Way of Doing Things', reducing dependence on individual personalities) and People.
business.title: Notable from the deck

outlook.body: Outlook: Stable; Strategy: Focus on sustainable energy and sugar production
outlook.title: Guidance / outlook

deepdive.thesis: Magadh Sugar & Energy Limited has been upgraded to 'IND A+' with a Stable Outlook by India Ratings and Research, reflecting its improved credit profile and stable business operations. The company's diversified revenue streams from sugar and energy segments contribute to its resilience. However, the industry's volatility and regulatory risks may impact its performance.

open.item: Expand Narkatiaganj sugar unit crushing capacity from 7,500 TCD to 10,000 TCD, going on steam by November-December 2024.
Narkatiaganj expansion carries total invested capital cost of ~Rs 141 crores and is expected to deliver EBITDA of not less than 25%.
Narkatiaganj steam-saving measures to reduce steam consumption from ~44.7% to 34.8%.
Convert Sidhwalia molasses-based distillery to a multi-feed (grain/maize/rice) distillery at a capital cost of ~Rs 32 crores.
Company plans to complete all announced capex projects (Narkatiaganj expansion and Sidhwalia multi-feed conversion) during the current financial year FY25.
With the Narkatiaganj capacity increase, crushing at that unit is expected to rise by 28% to 29%.
Execute varietal replacement plan to replace red-rot-infested CO 238 cane with CO0118 and CO9301, keeping any single variety between 30% and 40% next season to improve recovery.
Management intends to reduce debt to gain financial flexibility and lower finance costs, freeing capital for value-creating projects.
Post multi-feed conversion, Sidhwalia distillery (150 KLPD) can run up to 340 days and produce up to ~5.50 crore litres of ethanol annually.
Company sees scope to grow cane crushed from ~237 lakh quintals last season up to ~288 lakh quintals as saturation point not yet reached.
If government grants full freedom, company intends to shift product mix back toward roughly 90% B-heavy/juice and 10% C-heavy, subject to price economics.
Maize availability of ~1 lakh MT from Samastipur, Begusarai and Khagaria against a daily requirement of ~260 MT/day secures feedstock for the multi-feed distillery.
New ethanol policy restricting C-molasses usage limits distillery utilisation (not more than ~3.8-3.9 cr litres vs 5.5 cr potential), the key rationale for multi-feed conversion.
Bihar low-land flooding and red-rot infestation of CO 238 variety are flagged risks to cane recovery, mitigated via embankments and topography-based variety selection.

wtt.summary: Building track record — 1Q logged, no reconciled verdicts yet.
wtt.tone_latest: Confident and forward-leaning on capex delivery within FY25; management candidly owned the lower cane recovery (red-rot in CO 238) and flagged ethanol-policy and flooding constraints rather than glossing over them.
